chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: The 1933 road show with the Mills Brothers
summary: Redman's band toured East Coast theaters with the Mills Brothers and a full revue until John Mills's illness folded it.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So we come out of Connie's Inn and the next year, like 1933, we went on the road with a show with the Mills Brothers, one of the most fantastic shows, to me, road shows that has been ever put together. We had Ralph Brown who was a very good dancer in those days.

And we had a little comedy team, Red and Strugge. They used to do the lindy hop to 'Nagasaki'. And we had Myra Johnson. She used to be Fats Waller's vocalist. And we had Pete, Peaches and Duke, which was the neatest dance act I think I've ever seen, you know, and the Mills Brothers and, of course, the band.
That was a fantastic show. We played all the theaters all over the East Coast. We didn't go west.
Then after that that that broke up -- and John Mills got sick, you see, the Mills Brothers. That's when he died was that year. He got tuberculosis.
Yes, and when he got sick the show folded. Oh, we had a chorus line too.
We had a chorus line of 12 girls.
